articles.title: 7 Buzzer-Beater MLB Free Agency, Trade Predictions Before Lockout
articles.summary: The MLB offseason is on the clock, not because Opening Day is near, but because an imminent lockout will freeze all transactions at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1.
articles.body:
The MLB offseason is on the clock, not because Opening Day is near, but because an imminent lockout will freeze all transactions at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1.

With several of the market's top players signing in recent days, including Tarik Skubal, Trevor Rogers, Freddy Peralta and Teruaki Sato, there is a clear push by teams to get deals done before the uncertainty of the next CBA becomes a factor.

With that in mind, we've highlighted seven deals that could still be completed for teams looking for a buzzer-beater move.

It's a mix of free agency signings and trades, rooted in team needs, recent rumors and a fair amount of speculation.

Contract Prediction: Five years, $140 million

The starting pitching dominoes have begun falling in the wake of Tarik Skubal's massive contract with the New York Mets.

With Trevor Rogers (five years, $120 million) and Freddy Peralta (five years, $125 million) setting the market, Michael King is the remaining frontline-caliber arm who remains unsigned, and he has a solid case for a bigger payday than both of those pitchers.

King opted out of a $28 million salary for the 2027 season to become a free agent, and matching that figure over a new five-year deal would slot him ahead of those other signings in total money.

The Padres currently have Jhony Brito, Ryan Weiss and Ian Koenig penciled in behind Joe Musgrove and Randy Vásquez in their projected rotation , so there is clearly work to be done rebuilding the staff.

Put another way, if the Padres don't re-sign King, how do they replace him?

Contract Prediction: Five years, $120 million

The Blue Jays have been connected to a wide variety of high-profile free agents this offseason, but their interest in Seiya Suzuki dates back to September, when The Athletic reported they were expected to pursue him.

With a clear need for a middle-of-the-order bat and an upgrade at one of the corner outfield spots, Suzuki and Randy Arozarena are both logical candidates to be Toronto's splashy addition on the offensive side of things.

Now that a reunion with the Cubs is unlikely following their move to sign Teruaki Sato, Suzuki's market could come together quickly. If he is the Blue Jays' top target, they might push to get a deal done before the lockout.

After posting a 131 OPS+ with 26 home runs and a career-high 5.1 WAR in 2026, Suzuki should be able to secure a modest raise and a nine-figure payday on a long-term deal.

Contract Prediction: Two years, $30 million

The Cubs have already made a pair of splashy signings, adding Trevor Rogers to the starting rotation and Teruaki Sato to fill one of the corner outfield holes, but there is still work to be done rebuilding the starting rotation.

A reunion with deadline pickups Kevin Gausman or Clay Holmes remains a possibility, but they have also been speculatively linked to veteran Japanese League standout Hiromi Itoh.

The 29-year-old has spent six seasons with the Nippon Ham Fighters, posting a 2.91 ERA, 1.17 WHIP and 914 strikeouts in 1,008.2 innings. He stands out more for his command and pitchability than his stuff, but profiles as a viable No. 4 starter stateside.

His age and modest stuff mean he likely won't come close to matching the five-year, $80 million deal that Kaima Taira landed from the Blue Jays, and a $15 million AAV on a two-year contract fits the market for a solid back-end starter.

One way or another, expect Itoh to make his decision before lockout day.

Contract Prediction: Four years, $92 million

With new ownership set to take over, the Angels should have additional motivation to snap an ugly run of 11 straight losing seasons, and upgrading the lineup around Zach Neto and Mike Trout should be their top priority.

They used six different starting second basemen in 2026, and no one started more than 57 games at the position, so there is no one standing in the way of an outside addition.

Veteran second basemen have often faced a lackluster market in recent years, so Brandon Lowe may be motivated to accept a significant offer before the Dec. 1 lockout rather than wait.

The 32-year-old had a 121 OPS+ with 35 home runs for the Pirates in 2026 to win NL Silver Slugger honors, and he has been one of baseball's best offensive second basemen throughout his career.

A $23 million AAV would roughly match the figure from the qualifying offer he rejected at the start of the offseason.

Pittsburgh Pirates Acquire Jordan Westburg

To PIT: 3B Jordan Westburg To BAL: RHP Carmen Mlodzinski, OF Mitch Jebb

If the Pirates fail to re-sign Brandon Lowe, as we're predicting, they could quickly pivot to an alternative upgrade on the infield.

Targeting a third baseman would improve their infield defense after Nick Gonzales struggled at the hot corner (-15 DRS, -11 OAA in 2026). He has generally been a passable defender at second base, so shifting him back to his more natural defensive home would be a logical first step if the door closes on a Lowe reunion.

A Jordan Westburg-for-Carmen Mlodzinski swap looks like a potential win-win trade for both the Pirates and Orioles, addressing a need by dealing from an area of abundance. Both players are 27 years old, and both are controllable through the 2029 season.

Westburg was an All-Star in 2024, and he has a 116 OPS+ over 1,027 career plate appearances in the majors, but he missed the entire 2026 season recovering from Tommy John surgery.

Mlodzinski has a 3.77 ERA in 222 innings over the last two seasons bouncing between the rotation and the bullpen, and he made it clear he prefers to start last year when he was bumped to a relief role following Jared Jones' return.

Considering Westburg has proven more at the MLB level, the Pirates would likely have to sweeten the pot with a prospect piece, and Mitch Jebb is close to MLB ready with solid athleticism and versatility.

Contract Prediction: Two years, $40 million

Tyler Mahle was a completely different pitcher last year after joining the Braves in a trade deadline deal with the Giants:

SF: 18 GS, 5.13 ERA, 1.39 WHIP, 37 BB, 89 K, 94.2 IP, -0.1 WAR ATL: 9 GS, 1.99 ERA, 0.96 WHIP, 9 BB, 48 K, 54.1 IP, 1.8 WAR

He went on to toss a pair of gems in the NLWC (7.0 IP, 6 H, 1 ER) and NLDS (6.1 IP, 3 H, 1 ER), and now he stands as one of the more appealing starting pitchers left standing on a rapidly unfolding market.

His injury history and uneven performance last year will likely limit the length of his next contract, but he should earn a solid raise over the one-year, $10 million deal he signed last winter.

The same need for stability behind ace Chris Sale that led to the Mahle trade in August still exists for the Braves, and a reunion on a two-year deal with a solid raise might be enough to make both sides happy.

Chicago White Sox Acquire Shane McClanahan

To TB: OF Jaden Fauske, RHP Pierce George

With a $6.6 million projected salary in his final year of arbitration, Shane McClanahan stands to be one of the highest-paid players on the Tampa Bay roster in 2027.

The two-time All-Star returned after missing the entire 2024 and 2025 seasons with a solid campaign, posting a 3.36 ERA, 1.12 WHIP and 106 strikeouts in 118 innings, though his season again ended on the sidelines as he dealt with left forearm tightness.

The expectation is that he will be fully healthy to begin the 2027 season, and for a White Sox team in clear need of starting pitching upgrades, his ace-caliber upside is worth rolling the dice.

Because he can become a free agent after 2027, and because the lockout could shorten the season, his acquisition price shouldn't be prohibitively steep.

Jaden Fauske was frequently linked to the Rays throughout the predraft process in 2025 before going to the White Sox in the second round, and he would serve as a high-upside centerpiece, while Pierce George is a potential MLB-ready bullpen arm with strikeout stuff.

articles.title: Predicting Every MLB Team's 2027 Opening Day Lineup With Signings and Trades
articles.summary: The expectation of an imminent MLB lockout has sparked a flurry of activity in free agency in recent days, with teams looking to make a splash before transactions grind to a halt.
articles.body:
The expectation of an imminent MLB lockout has sparked a flurry of activity in free agency in recent days, with teams looking to make a splash before transactions grind to a halt.

That makes this the perfect time for our first deep dive into each team's potential Opening Day lineup for the 2027 season.

Veterans under contract and established young talent served as the foundation for projected lineups, and the gaps were filled in from there with up-and-coming prospects and logical outside additions.

Note: Names in bold indicate a projected trade or free-agent signing.

ARI | ATH | ATL | BAL | BOS | CHC | CIN | CLE | COL | CWS | DET | HOU | KC | LAA | LAD | MIA | MIL | MIN | NYM | NYY | PHI | PIT | SD | SEA | SF | STL | TB | TEX | TOR | WSH

SS Geraldo Perdomo RF Corbin Carroll C Gabriel Moreno DH Lars Nootbaar 3B Nolan Arenado 1B Nathaniel Lowe CF Jordan Lawlar LF Ryan Waldschmidt 2B Demetrio Crisantes (R)

Key Prediction: Will we finally see a Ketel Marte trade this winter? The three-time All-Star would need to waive his 10-and-5 veto rights, but it felt like we were moving toward a change of scenery being good for all involved last year. Moving him would clear a path for top prospect Demetrio Crisantes, who hit .292/.377/.477 in the upper minors before a solid run in the Arizona Fall League.

CF Henry Bolte 1B Nick Kurtz C Shea Langeliers RF Lawrence Butler DH Brent Rooker LF Tyler Soderstrom 2B Zack Gelof SS Jacob Wilson 3B Tommy White

Key Prediction: The versatility of Zack Gelof gives the Athletics some flexibility filling out the lineup, as he can handle second base, third base or center field. Slugger Tommy White hit .303/.353/.465 with 17 doubles, 10 home runs and 64 RBI in 76 games between Double-A and Triple-A last season, and after getting his feet wet with 56 games in the majors, he could push for the third base job with a strong spring.

DH Drake Baldwin RF Ronald Acuña Jr. 1B Matt Olson CF Michael Harris II 3B Austin Riley SS Mauricio Dubón 2B Ozzie Albies LF Mike Yastrzemski C Sean Murphy

Key Prediction: The Braves could kick the tires on veteran J.P. Crawford or explore a trade for someone like Zach Neto or Jeremy Peña if they become available, but right now a reunion with Mauricio Dubón looks like the most obvious approach to addressing the hole at shortstop. The 32-year-old set career-high marks in home runs (12) and RBI (73) in a super-utility role last year.

Buzzer-Beater Predictions Before Lockout 🔮

2B Jackson Holliday 1B Pete Alonso SS Gunnar Henderson 3B Christian Encarnacion-Strand C Samuel Basallo DH Coby Mayo RF Tyler O'Neill LF Dylan Beavers CF Colton Cowser

Key Prediction: The performance of scrapheap pickup Christian Encarnacion-Strand (213 PA, 134 OPS+, 11 HR, 39 RBI) has created a logjam at third base, and a healthy Jordan Westburg could be the trade chip that helps the O's bolster their starting rotation. Keep reading for his projected landing spot.

LF Roman Anthony C Adley Rutschman DH Jake Bauers 1B Willson Contreras RF Wilyer Abreu CF Ceddanne Rafaela 3B Caleb Durbin SS Trevor Story 2B Curtis Mead

Key Prediction: The Red Sox opted to tender a contract to Jarren Duran, but there is still a high likelihood he is traded before the start of the season, especially with the addition of Jake Bauers clogging up designated hitter opportunities. The other big question in Boston is how quickly top prospect Franklin Arias will be ready, but Curtis Mead and Trevor Story will likely start the year manning the middle infield spots.

CF Pete Crow-Armstrong 2B Nico Hoerner 3B Alex Bregman 1B Michael Busch RF Teruaki Sato (R) DH Pedro Ramírez LF Matt Shaw SS Dansby Swanson C Miguel Amaya

Key Prediction: The Cubs have had a busy week, signing Trevor Rogers (5/$120M) and Teruaki Sato (6/$120M) to nine-figure deals, likely closing the door on a reunion with Seiya Suzuki in the process. The front office could still hunt for this year's version of the Michael Conforto signing, but leaving a corner outfield spot and designated hitter open for Matt Shaw, Pedro Ramírez and Kevin Alcántara to battle for playing time makes a ton of sense.

LF Sam Antonacci 2B Chase Meidroth 1B Munetaka Murakami 3B Miguel Vargas DH Andrew Benintendi C Kyle Teel CF Tristan Peters SS Colson Montgomery RF Braden Montgomery

Key Prediction: The focus for the White Sox this winter is going to be bolstering the pitching staff, as they already have an enviable young offensive core in place without a glaring hole to fill. Expect to see deadline pickup Brenton Doyle platoon with Tristan Peters in center field, while a right-handed hitting DH bat to pair with Andrew Benintendi could be on the shopping list.

RF Héctor Rodríguez SS Elly De La Cruz 1B Sal Stewart LF JJ Bleday DH Spencer Steer CF Daulton Varsho C Tyler Stephenson 2B Matt McLain 3B Ke'Bryan Hayes

Key Prediction: With TJ Friedl gone and Noelvi Marte regressing significantly, the Reds outfield is loaded with question marks alongside JJ Bleday. Prospects Héctor Rodriguez and Carlos Jorge will likely get a long look for a spot on the Opening Day roster, but Cincinnati could be the perfect landing spot for Daulton Varsho, with his power-centric offensive game and elite glove in center field.

CF Steven Kwan RF Chase DeLauter 3B José Ramírez LF Jo Adell 1B Ralphy Velazquez (R) DH Travis Bazzana 2B Angel Genao C Patrick Bailey SS Brayan Rocchio

Key Prediction: The Guardians already made their big lineup splash when they acquired Jo Adell from the Angels last summer, and with a projected $9.6 million arbitration salary he will be one of the highest-paid players on the team in 2027. The big potential addition is top prospect Ralphy Velazquez, who hit .290/.379/.548 with 29 home runs and 93 RBI in 121 games between Double-A and Triple-A.

LF Jake McCarthy CF Cole Carrigg C Hunter Goodman 1B TJ Rumfield RF Mickey Moniak DH Charlie Condon (R) 3B Kyle Karros 2B Adael Amador SS Ezequiel Tovar

Key Prediction: The Rockies have quietly assembled a solid offensive core with Hunter Goodman, TJ Rumfield, Jake McCarthy, Cole Carrigg and Mickey Moniak tallying a combined 9.4 WAR last season. Former first-round pick Charlie Condon has a chance to join them in 2027 after hitting .273/.390/.514 with 27 home runs and 98 RBI in 130 games at Triple-A.

SS Kevin McGonigle 2B Hao-Yu Lee LF Riley Greene C Dillon Dingler DH Kerry Carpenter 1B Spencer Torkelson 3B Colt Keith CF Max Clark RF Zyhir Hope (R)

Key Prediction: Whether he's on the Opening Day roster or starts the year at Triple-A, it's only a matter of time before Zyhir Hope joins Riley Greene and Max Clark in what could be one of the most productive outfields in baseball. The centerpiece of the Tarik Skubal trade with the Dodgers, Hope hit .287/.367/.513 with 29 home runs and 111 RBI in 124 games at Double-A, and he has the polish to jump over the Triple-A level.

SS Jeremy Peña LF Yordan Alvarez DH Isaac Paredes 2B Jose Altuve 3B Carlos Correa 1B Christian Walker CF Lucas Spence C Yainer Diaz RF Cam Smith

Key Prediction: The Astros are once again facing a potential infield logjam that would force Yordan Alvarez to play primarily left field when everyone is healthy, but that worked itself out last year when Carlos Correa missed the bulk of the season. Despite no new name penciled into the projected lineup, there will almost certainly be an outside addition of some sort in the outfield, though Lucas Spence showed enough in September to get a look as the primary center fielder.

C Carter Jensen SS Bobby Witt Jr. RF Jac Caglianone DH Salvador Perez LF Teoscar Hernández 1B Vinnie Pasquantino 3B Alec Bohm 2B Michael Massey CF Carson Roccaforte (R)

Key Prediction: The Teoscar Hernández prediction is the immediate attention grabber, but don't overlook Carson Roccaforte as an in-house replacement for Kyle Isbel capable of a far more significant impact. The 24-year-old had an .857 OPS with 35 home runs and 32 steals between Double-A and Triple-A last year, and he is widely regarded as one of the best defensive outfielders in the minors.

SS Zach Neto LF Mike Trout 2B Brandon Lowe DH Vaughn Grissom 1B Nolan Schanuel RF Wade Meckler CF Josh Lowe C Jonah Heim 3B Nolan Gorman

Key Prediction: With a new ownership group set to take over, don't be surprised if the Angels look to make a splash this offseason, and adding Brandon Lowe as a reliable run producer would be a great first step. They also look like the perfect team to take a flier on Nolan Gorman after he was non-tendered by the Cardinals, as the 26-year-old former top prospect potentially still has some untapped upside.

DH Shohei Ohtani CF Andy Pages 1B Freddie Freeman C Will Smith 3B Max Muncy SS Mookie Betts RF Kyle Tucker LF Josue De Paula (R) 2B Tommy Edman

Key Prediction: With a .323/.500/.581 line in 42 plate appearances as a September call-up following a standout season at Double-A, and some surprise playoff exposure, Josue De Paula is ready for a big league role. Dumping Teoscar Hernández's salary is the most obvious approach to clearing a path, though the two could also platoon to start the year.

2B Xavier Edwards LF Heriberto Hernández SS Otto Lopez RF Griffin Conine 1B Kyle Stowers 3B Javier Sanoja DH Owen Caissie C Joe Mack CF Cam Cannarella (R)

Key Prediction: With Jakob Marsee expected to start the year on the injured list while he continues his recovery from elbow surgery in October, there is an opportunity for rising prospect Cam Cannarella. The 23-year-old was the No. 43 overall pick in the 2025 draft, and he hit .324/.422/.512 with 38 extra-base hits and 21 steals in 98 games while reaching Triple-A in his first full professional season.

2B Brice Turang CF Garrett Mitchell LF Jackson Chourio C William Contreras DH Christian Yelich 1B Andrew Vaughn RF Sal Frelick SS Cooper Pratt 3B Joey Ortiz

Key Prediction: The Brewers could welcome an influx of young talent to the majors in 2027, with Jesús Made and Andrew Fischer potentially manning the corner infield spots before season's end. That said, it will likely be the status quo to start the year, unless they come to terms on another pre-debut extension like the ones they handed out to Jackson Chourio and Cooper Pratt.

RF Luke Keaschall 2B Luis Arraez DH Byron Buxton C Ryan Jeffers 1B Kody Clemens 3B Brooks Lee CF Walker Jenkins (R) SS Kaelen Culpepper (R) LF Emmanuel Rodriguez (R)

Key Prediction: With Sonny Gray signed, Royce Lewis traded and Bailey Ober and Trevor Larnach non-tendered, it has already been a busy offseason of retooling for the Twins. Walker Jenkins, Kaelen Culpepper and Emmanuel Rodriguez all made their MLB debuts last season and should factor heavily into the 2027 plans, while a reunion with Luis Arraez would help stabilize the lineup while they settle in.

SS Francisco Lindor LF Juan Soto 3B Bo Bichette RF Carson Benge 1B Paul Goldschmidt CF A.J. Ewing DH Jorge Polanco 2B Marcus Semien C Francisco Alvarez

Key Prediction: The Mets still have significant work to do rebuilding the pitching staff around Tarik Skubal, Nolan McLean and Devin Williams, so the focus of their remaining offseason moves will likely be on the mound. Jared Young and Brett Baty will be platoon options on the right side of the infield, while Mark Vientos is still capable of playing his way into a regular role as well.

DH Ben Rice LF Cody Bellinger RF Aaron Judge 1B Luis García Jr. CF Spencer Jones C Carson Kelly SS George Lombard Jr. 3B Ryan McMahon 2B Anthony Volpe

Key Prediction: The Yankees got a .196 average and .600 OPS from the catcher position last season, including a 74 OPS+ from incumbent starter Austin Wells. With a .122/.192/.244 line against left-handed pitching, they at least need to find him a right-handed hitting platoon partner, and veteran Carson Kelly would be a clear upgrade.

DH Kyle Schwarber SS Trea Turner 1B Bryce Harper RF Randy Arozarena LF Brandon Marsh C J.T. Realmuto 2B Bryson Stott 3B Aidan Miller (R) CF Justin Crawford

Key Prediction: The Phillies have a glaring need for a right-handed hitting outfielder, and should be considered a prime landing spot for Randy Arozarena or Seiya Suzuki. The more compelling prediction here is Aidan Miller making his MLB debut as the Opening Day third baseman. The 22-year-old saw his development derailed by injuries in 2026, but he made up for lost time with a .327/.557/.481 line over 79 plate appearances in the Arizona Fall League while playing third base.

SS Konnor Griffin CF Oneil Cruz RF Bryan Reynolds 3B Jordan Westburg 1B Ryan O'Hearn DH Esmerlyn Valdez LF Ian Happ C Rafael Flores Jr. 2B Nick Gonzales

Key Prediction: Buying low on Jordan Westburg, who is controllable through the 2029 season and not far removed from being an All-Star in 2024, could give the Pirates a low-cost replacement for Brandon Lowe on the infield. With a .300/.380/.512 line over 296 career plate appearances at PNC Park and Pittsburgh roots, Ian Happ looks like the ideal target to round out the lineup.

RF Fernando Tatis Jr. 2B Jake Cronenworth 3B Manny Machado CF Jackson Merrill SS Xander Bogaerts DH Jarren Duran 1B Gavin Sheets LF Dustin Harris C Ethan Salas (R)

Key Prediction: The Padres got solid production from Dustin Harris and Samad Taylor in a left field platoon down the stretch last season, but they still look like one of the most logical landing spots for Jarren Duran. He is penciled in here as designated hitter, but can also provide insurance to those largely unproven options in left field and a capable center field backup to Jackson Merrill if he misses time.

2B Gleyber Torres DH Bryce Eldridge 3B Matt Chapman 1B Rafael Devers RF Jung Hoo Lee LF Casey Schmitt SS Willy Adames CF Drew Gilbert C Daniel Susac

Key Prediction: The Giants have some flexibility in how they attack shoring up their lineup, as Casey Schmitt could potentially handle second base or left field, though his best position is still third base. It's not out of the question to think they could bring aboard Gleyber Torres on the same one-year, $12 million deal they gave to Luis Arraez last offseason.

LF Brendan Donovan RF Dominic Canzone CF Julio Rodríguez C Cal Raleigh 1B Josh Naylor 3B Maikel Garcia DH Lazaro Montes (R) 2B Cole Young SS Colt Emerson

Key Prediction: The Mariners already added one significant new piece in Maikel Garcia, and Brendan Donovan almost feels like a newcomer himself after playing a grand total of 39 games in 2026. Colt Emerson is set to be turned loose at shortstop, while Lazaro Montes could go a long way toward replacing Randy Arozarena's run production if he delivers on his power potential.

2B JJ Wetherholt DH Iván Herrera 1B Alec Burleson RF Jordan Walker LF Joshua Baez (R) C Leo Bernal (R) 3B Edmundo Sosa SS Masyn Winn CF Nathan Church

Key Prediction: The youth movement is underway in St. Louis, and they have assembled a solid young core with Jordan Walker, Alec Burleson, JJ Wetherholt and Masyn Winn, while Leo Bernal and Joshua Baez both showed flashes in their debuts. A reliable, versatile veteran like Edmundo Sosa could be the perfect complementary pickup, and he could compete with Thomas Saggese for the third base job.

DH Yandy Díaz 1B Jonathan Aranda 3B Junior Caminero C Liam Hicks LF Chandler Simpson RF Victor Mesa Jr. 2B Richie Palacios CF Jonny Deluca SS Taylor Walls

Key Prediction: There have been some rumblings that the Rays might consider moving center fielder Jonny DeLuca this winter, but they're not going to move him unless they get something of significance in return. For now, the status quo looks like the most logical prediction on the offensive side of things, especially with multiple decisions to make in the rotation following the departures of Nick Martinez and Freddy Peralta.

CF Wyatt Langford SS Corey Seager DH Josh Jung RF Brandon Nimmo LF Taylor Ward 3B Ezequiel Durán 2B Jazz Chisholm Jr. 1B Jake Burger C Danny Jansen

Key Prediction: The Rangers' front office identified getting younger and more athletic as the focus of the offseason, and for all his ups and downs, few players across baseball check the athleticism box more decisively than Jazz Chisholm Jr. with his 30/30 upside. If he is available on a one-year, prove-it deal, the Rangers should make a serious push to sign him.

CF Brett Bateman LF Nathan Lukes 1B Vladimir Guerrero Jr. RF Seiya Suzuki C Alejandro Kirk 3B Kazuma Okamoto DH Ketel Marte 2B Ernie Clement SS Andrés Giménez

Key Prediction: The Blue Jays have been circling Seiya Suzuki since before the offseason even started, and he remains a logical fit in the middle of their lineup and filling a hole at a corner outfield spot. The Ketel Marte fit is more speculative, but this is a Toronto organization clearly looking to make a splash after last year's disappointing finish, and Marte would be a major addition to an already dangerous lineup.

DH James Wood 2B CJ Abrams RF Dylan Crews LF Daylen Lile 1B Ty France 3B Brady House SS J.P. Crawford C Keibert Ruiz CF Jacob Young

Key Prediction: Despite falling off after a competitive start, the Nationals still feel like a team on the rise. Improving the starting rotation is their No. 1 need, but there is also a void to fill at first base and a potential hole to plug at shortstop if CJ Abrams makes a full-time move to second base. Former teammates Ty France and J.P. Crawford won't break the bank, but could go a long way toward solidifying the starting nine.

articles.title: Pirates trade Henry Davis to Diamondbacks
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Pirates have made their first notable move of the offseason.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Pirates have made their first notable move of the offseason. Catcher Henry Davis has been traded to the Arizona Diamondbacks for utilityman Tim Tawa, a source confirmed to Pittsburgh Baseball Now.

Davis was selected by the Pirates with the first overall pick in the 2021 draft. He made his MLB debut two years later and has totaled 283 games with Pittsburgh over the last four seasons. Davis owns a .178/.265/.300 batting line with 27 doubles, 25 home runs, 89 RBI and eight stolen bases.

The 27-year-old appeared in a career-high 97 games for the Pirates this season. He batted .172/.272/.313 batting line with six doubles, 10 home runs, 38 RBI and three stolen bases.

While Davis hasn't had much success offensively in the big leagues, he's established himself as a strong defensive catcher. Davis appeared in 94 games behind the plate this season and totaled eight defensive runs saved. He also led all MLB catchers with a 45.9% caught stealing rate.

articles.title: A.J. Ewing’s $95 million contract extension gets big Mets update
articles.summary: With the New York Mets signing star free agent Tarik Skubal to a $450 million contract, the team has made other moves that could be overshadowed now that th...
articles.body:
With the New York Mets signing star free agent Tarik Skubal to a $450 million contract, the team has made other moves that could be overshadowed now that the ball club landed the biggest target in the market. One being how the Mets signed A.J. Ewing to a $95 million contract extension that has just received new details on the deal.

With the deal being made official Friday, MLB insider Jorge Castillo at ESPN says that the $95 million is guaranteed, and it comes with a club option worth $25 million for the ninth year in the contract.

"A.J. Ewing's eight-year contract extension with the Mets is official. It's for $95 million guaranteed with a $25 million club option for a ninth year," Castillo wrote on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

This past season was Ewing's rookie year with New York, where he recorded a .252 batting average to go along with 11 home runs and 43 RBIs. Ewing was one of the bright spots for the Mets last season, joining a rookie group along with pitcher Nolan McLean and outfielder Carson Benge.

More on the Mets signing A.J. Ewing to a contract extension

Benge's contract extension with the Mets was a "big deal," according to SNY insider Chelsea Jane, saying that a pre-arbitration deal hasn't happened like this since David Wright, saying, "This one is bigger than that.

"It's a big deal also because it's a reminder of how much their system has produced in recent years. A.J. Ewing wasn't even the headliner of last year's rookie class…He came up," Jane said. "He played like a Gold Glove center fielder. He showed flashes of being the leadoff man of the future, navigated some ups and downs, and some growth. He's 22 years old. This deal buys out his pre-arb years, his arb-years, and gets him into free agency, and that's a big deal for the Mets."

With Jane later teasing that the team could do these types of deals with McLean and Benge, it remains to be seen what further moves they make, as while Skubal was a huge get, the team looks to continue to make an impact this offseason.

articles.title: Diamondbacks trade Tim Tawa to Pirates
articles.summary: The Snakes add catcher Henry Davis.
articles.body:
Hot stove season is in full swing ahead of the potential MLB lockout scheduled to start on Wednesday. The Diamondbacks have been relatively quiet so far, trading for RHP Johan Oviedo and non-tendering Blake Walston and Andrew Saalfrank. But they made a second move on Friday morning.

Jeff Passan reported that the Diamondbacks traded utilityman Tim Tawa to the Pittsburgh Pirates for catcher Henry Davis.

Tawa appeared in 104 games for the Dbacks in 2026, slashing .240/.297/.393 with 11 home runs. He also took "utilityman" seriously, as he played at every position except catcher, shortstop and pitcher. He mostly appeared at first base (406 total innings), but also saw a decent chunk of time in left and center field.

Davis was drafted first-overall out of Louisville in the 2021 MLB Draft. He made his MLB debut on June 19, 2023 and hit .213/.302/.351 with seven home runs across 62 games in his first season. Unfortunately, he hasn't really taken off since. In 2026, Davis played 97 games and slashed .172/.272/.313 with 10 home runs. However, his walk percentage was up from 6.4% in 2025 to 9.4% in 2026, and his strikeout percentage went down from 26.9% in 2025 to 21.1% in 2026. While those numbers aren't great, they could be encouraging. In total across four seasons, he has played in 283 games and hit just .178/.265/.300 with 25 home runs.

Davis is known more for his defense, though. In 2026, he committed four errors — two fielding and two throwing — and posted a 3 FRV (Fielding Run Value). He also posted an 8 DRS (Defensive Runs Saved) in both 2026 and 2025.

This is a developing story and AZ Snake Pit will provide more information as it becomes available.
